To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) there are a large number of replicated web pages, (ii) there are also a large number of hyperlinked document collections that are being replicated, and (iii) we have developed an efficient algorithm to identify replicated pages and collections, and we have used this algorithm to improve web crawls and a search engine ranking function.

(1) the web is full of replicated documents and document collections; (2) it is easy to identify such replicas from an input set of several million web pages, and (3) the identification of these replicas is useful to improve web crawls, web search engines, and archiving

1) the replication ratio for web documents is about 10% for the web as a whole, but it can be higher than 50% for some document collections (such Linux FAQs); 2) the average replication factor for web pages is about 1.2 (i.e., 1 page has about 0.8 replicas); 3) there are many replicated document collections on the web; 4) the replication factor for document collections is higher than that of documents;
